title: Trump Administration Files Emergency SCOTUS Application to Enforce Mail-In Voting Restrictions
detail: The Trump administration asked the Supreme Court on July 27, 2026 to intervene and allow full implementation of Trump's March 2026 executive order restricting mail-in voting, 99 days before the November midterms. The order requires the US Postal Service to compile lists of voters eligible to receive mail ballots and gives it new power to block delivery to anyone not listed. The emergency application followed a 2-1 ruling by the 1st US Circuit Court of Appeals leaving in place a Massachusetts federal judge's order that paused the policy in 23 states and D.C. Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson, handling emergency appeals from that circuit, ordered plaintiff states to respond by August 3.

media.caption: Trump administration asks Supreme Court to allow mail-in voting restrictions ahead of midterms
